title: Introduce yourself
objective: Give a simple three-part introduction in your own words.
opening: Hi, it is nice to meet you. Tell me your name, where you are from, and one thing you enjoy.

criteria.label: Say your name clearly.
Share where you are from or live.
Add one personal detail you enjoy sharing.

beats: Hi, it is nice to meet you. Tell me your name, where you are from, and one thing you enjoy.
Ask one easy follow-up about the personal detail.
Thank the learner and close warmly.
scaffold: You can say: My name is ___. I am from ___. I enjoy ___.
transfer: Use the same three-part introduction the next time you meet someone new.
recovery: If the learner pauses, show the three sentence starter and invite them to fill the blanks.
Never challenge, score, or pressure the learner during this first practice.
variants: What do you enjoy about that?
How did you first become interested in it?
What would you like someone new to know about you?

title: Tell me about yourself
objective: Introduce yourself with a relevant story and one concrete strength.
opening: Tell me about yourself and what interests you about this role.

criteria.label: Connect your experience to the role.
Give a specific example of your contribution.
Finish with why this opportunity fits.

beats: Tell me about yourself and what interests you about this role.
What did you personally contribute?
How would that help you in this role?
What would you need to learn first?
Close naturally after the user proposes a next step.
objections: What did you personally contribute?
How would that help you in this role?
What would you need to learn first?
scaffold: Present → evidence → why this role. Use your own facts.
transfer: Practice your opening before your next interview.
recovery: If the user gets stuck, ask one simpler question without answering for them.
If the user asks for clarification, explain the question and let them try again.
variants: What did you personally contribute?
How would that help you in this role?
What would you need to learn first?

title: Explain your experience with an example
objective: Explain a specific situation, your action, and the result.
opening: Tell me about a time you solved a difficult problem.

criteria.label: Establish the situation briefly.
Distinguish your own action from the team's.
Describe a result without inventing numbers.

beats: Tell me about a time you solved a difficult problem.
What part was your responsibility?
What changed because of your action?
What would you do differently now?
Close naturally after the user proposes a next step.
objections: What part was your responsibility?
What changed because of your action?
What would you do differently now?
scaffold: Situation → your action → result. A small real example is enough.
transfer: Write down one real example you can use in an interview.
recovery: If the user gets stuck, ask one simpler question without answering for them.
If the user asks for clarification, explain the question and let them try again.
variants: What part was your responsibility?
What changed because of your action?
What would you do differently now?

title: Think under interview pressure
objective: Clarify an unexpected question and answer honestly.
opening: You are given a project you have never done before. How would you begin?

criteria.label: Clarify the uncertainty or name an assumption.
Explain a reasonable approach.
Acknowledge what you do not yet know.

beats: You are given a project you have never done before. How would you begin?
What if that first step fails?
Why would you choose that approach?
What information would change your answer?
Close naturally after the user proposes a next step.
objections: What if that first step fails?
Why would you choose that approach?
What information would change your answer?
scaffold: Pause. Name what you know, then one sensible next step.
transfer: Use a brief thinking pause before your next unfamiliar question.
recovery: If the user gets stuck, ask one simpler question without answering for them.
If the user asks for clarification, explain the question and let them try again.
variants: What if that first step fails?
Why would you choose that approach?
What information would change your answer?

title: Give a clear work update
objective: Give the headline, the blocker, and a useful next step.
opening: What changed, and do you need anything from me?

criteria.label: Lead with the current status.
Include only the relevant change or blocker.
Name an owner and next action.

beats: What changed, and do you need anything from me?
I only have thirty seconds. What matters most?
What do you need from me?
What happens next, and who owns it?
Close naturally after the user proposes a next step.
objections: I only have thirty seconds. What matters most?
What do you need from me?
What happens next, and who owns it?
transfer: Bring a three-line cue card to your next standup.
recovery: If the user gets stuck, ask one simpler question without answering for them.
If the user asks for clarification, explain the question and let them try again.
variants: I only have thirty seconds. What matters most?
What do you need from me?
What happens next, and who owns it?

title: Disagree in a meeting
objective: Acknowledge a view, explain your concern, and offer an alternative.
opening: I think we should ship this week and deal with the remaining issues later. What do you think?

criteria.label: Acknowledge the reason behind the other view.
State a specific concern respectfully.
Offer an alternative with a reason.

beats: I think we should ship this week and deal with the remaining issues later. What do you think?
We cannot afford another delay. What do you suggest?
Why is your alternative better?
What compromise could we try?
Close naturally after the user proposes a next step.
objections: We cannot afford another delay. What do you suggest?
Why is your alternative better?
What compromise could we try?
scaffold: I understand ___; my concern is ___; could we try ___?
transfer: Prepare one alternative before raising a concern in your next meeting.
recovery: If the user gets stuck, ask one simpler question without answering for them.
If the user asks for clarification, explain the question and let them try again.
variants: We cannot afford another delay. What do you suggest?
Why is your alternative better?
What compromise could we try?

title: Ask for a raise
objective: Make a clear request, support it with evidence, and agree on a next step.
opening: What did you want to discuss about your role?

criteria.label: State a specific request.
Support it with a relevant contribution.
Respond to the objection and propose a next step.

beats: What did you want to discuss about your role?
The budget is tight this quarter. What would you suggest?
Your role has not changed. Why an adjustment now?
What evidence should we review together?
Close naturally after the user proposes a next step.
objections: The budget is tight this quarter. What would you suggest?
Your role has not changed. Why an adjustment now?
What evidence should we review together?
scaffold: Request → result of your work → question about a workable next step.
transfer: Write one real achievement and one question for your manager.
recovery: If the user gets stuck, ask one simpler question without answering for them.
If the user asks for clarification, explain the question and let them try again.
variants: The budget is tight this quarter. What would you suggest?
Your role has not changed. Why an adjustment now?
What evidence should we review together?

title: Set a boundary
objective: State a clear limit and hold it through one objection.
opening: Could you take over my work again this evening? I know it is short notice.

criteria.label: State the limit clearly.
Give a brief reason without undermining the limit.
Maintain the limit after pushback.

beats: Could you take over my work again this evening? I know it is short notice.
It would only take you an hour. Could you make an exception?
What can you help with instead?
Who else could I ask?
Close naturally after the user proposes a next step.
objections: It would only take you an hour. Could you make an exception?
What can you help with instead?
Who else could I ask?
scaffold: I cannot ___; I can ___ if useful. You do not owe an elaborate explanation.
transfer: Choose one small boundary to state clearly this week.
recovery: If the user gets stuck, ask one simpler question without answering for them.
If the user asks for clarification, explain the question and let them try again.
variants: It would only take you an hour. Could you make an exception?
What can you help with instead?
Who else could I ask?

title: Explain a mistake
objective: Own a mistake, explain the impact, and propose a repair.
opening: I noticed a problem with the handover. Can you explain what happened?

criteria.label: Own your part without shifting blame.
State the known impact without guessing.
Propose a repair and prevention step.

beats: I noticed a problem with the handover. Can you explain what happened?
Who was affected?
How can we fix it now?
How will you prevent a repeat?
Close naturally after the user proposes a next step.
objections: Who was affected?
How can we fix it now?
How will you prevent a repeat?
scaffold: What happened → my part → impact → repair.
transfer: Bring a concrete repair proposal when you raise a problem.
recovery: If the user gets stuck, ask one simpler question without answering for them.
If the user asks for clarification, explain the question and let them try again.
variants: Who was affected?
How can we fix it now?
How will you prevent a repeat?

title: Ask for clarity
objective: Identify what is unclear and confirm an actionable expectation.
opening: Please get the usual materials ready for the meeting.

criteria.label: Name the specific missing information.
Ask a direct, useful question.
Confirm the next action or expectation.

beats: Please get the usual materials ready for the meeting.
You have done this before. What is unclear?
What do you need to know first?
How will you confirm we mean the same thing?
Close naturally after the user proposes a next step.
objections: You have done this before. What is unclear?
What do you need to know first?
How will you confirm we mean the same thing?
scaffold: To get this right, do you mean ___ or ___?
transfer: Ask one specific clarification instead of guessing in your next task.
recovery: If the user gets stuck, ask one simpler question without answering for them.
If the user asks for clarification, explain the question and let them try again.
variants: You have done this before. What is unclear?
What do you need to know first?
How will you confirm we mean the same thing?

title: Pitch your big idea
objective: Explain the problem, proposal, value, and next step.
opening: You have my attention. What is your idea, and why should it matter?

criteria.label: Define a concrete problem.
Explain the proposal and its value.
Ask for a clear next step.

beats: You have my attention. What is your idea, and why should it matter?
I do not see the benefit yet. Who needs this?
How is that different from what exists?
What small test would you run first?
Close naturally after the user proposes a next step.
objections: I do not see the benefit yet. Who needs this?
How is that different from what exists?
What small test would you run first?
scaffold: Problem → idea → value → small next step.
transfer: Test your opening with a peer and ask what they understood.
recovery: If the user gets stuck, ask one simpler question without answering for them.
If the user asks for clarification, explain the question and let them try again.
variants: I do not see the benefit yet. Who needs this?
How is that different from what exists?
What small test would you run first?

title: Meet someone new
objective: Introduce yourself, share something specific, and ask a genuine question.
opening: Hi, I do not think we have met. What brought you here?

criteria.label: Offer a brief, specific introduction.
Respond to something the partner actually said.
Ask a genuine follow-up and respect their time.

beats: Hi, I do not think we have met. What brought you here?
I am just here with a friend. How about you?
That sounds interesting. What got you into it?
I need to head off soon. It was nice meeting you.
Close naturally after the user proposes a next step.
objections: I am just here with a friend. How about you?
That sounds interesting. What got you into it?
I need to head off soon. It was nice meeting you.
scaffold: Share one thing about yourself, then ask about something they mentioned.
transfer: Introduce yourself to one relevant peer this week.
recovery: If the user gets stuck, ask one simpler question without answering for them.
If the user asks for clarification, explain the question and let them try again.
variants: I am just here with a friend. How about you?
That sounds interesting. What got you into it?
I need to head off soon. It was nice meeting you.

title: Open a presentation or toast
objective: Open with a clear point and a reason the audience should care.
opening: Imagine your audience is ready. How would you begin?

criteria.label: Make the main point clear.
Connect it to the audience.
Give the opening a clear direction.

beats: Imagine your audience is ready. How would you begin?
Why should this matter to this audience?
Could you make that more specific?
What would you want us to remember?
Close naturally after the user proposes a next step.
objections: Why should this matter to this audience?
Could you make that more specific?
What would you want us to remember?
scaffold: One point → why it matters here → where you are taking us.
transfer: Say your opening aloud once before the real event.
recovery: If the user gets stuck, ask one simpler question without answering for them.
If the user asks for clarification, explain the question and let them try again.
variants: Why should this matter to this audience?
Could you make that more specific?
What would you want us to remember?
